messages:
dana-support: FYI escalating for AcmeRetail — they see spikes in latency and intermittent 403s. They claim their app is pinned to region=us-west but requests keep landing in eu-west. Logs show x-rr-region: eu-west and token errors (issuer mismatch). Repro steps they gave below.

Tom-cs: ACK, thanks. Any quick ones we can run before we escalate to infra?

sanjay-eng: Can you paste a curl + headers and a minimal repro? Also need traceroute from their on-prem edge to our endpoint. Curious if this is TGW/peering routing preference or SNAT.

eli-onprem: Pasting the minimal repro and a couple of captures from their edge (they sanitized IPs).

eli-onprem: ```
# curl they run (sanitized)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-rr-region: eu-west
< x-request-id: r-xyz

# traceroute from on-prem edge to api.redwood.example (last hops)
 8  10.200.1.1 (edge-gw)  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.2 ms
 9  52.48.10.11 (transit)  10.3 ms  10.2 ms  10.1 ms
10  ec2-34-253-10-11.eu-west-1.compute (our front)  48.3 ms  48.1 ms  48.2 ms

# tcpdump at edge showing SNAT: source rewritten to 3.120.45.2 -> upstream shows eu-west pref
```

maya-net: Hmm looks like the path ends up in eu-west. Do they have a Transit Gateway or TGW peering? If their SD-WAN advertises a default route into the provider with higher local-pref, AWS route propagation could prefer the eu transit. Can you get the AWS route table/route table propagation from their VPC side or the TGW attachment? Also check whether they’re using an egress proxy that rewrites the X-Region header based on source IP geolocation.

sanjay-eng: Another quick test: can they force the SNI/Host to the us-west VIP? If that returns us-west we know it's DNS/anycast steering vs routing. Also request a sample of the auth error payload — the issuer claim usually includes region if we sign tokens per-region.

eli-onprem: They ran a quick dig and SNI check:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.example
34.253.10.11  # resolves to eu-west VIP from their resolver

# openssl s_client -connect 34.253.10.11:443 -servername api.redwood.example 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,6p'
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
subject=/CN=api.redwood.example
issuer=/CN=redwood-api-eu
```

eli-onprem: So DNS/anycast is returning an eu VIP into their path. They say their resolver is internal and tends to prefer upstream resolver which gets eu answers.

maya-net: That nails it — two possible layers: (1) DNS/anycast is steering them to EU; (2) on-prem egress is then SNATing via a path that hits our eu ingress. If tokens are region-scoped—403 is expected. For short-term mitigation we can add a token-agnostic fallback on the edge (allow issuer mismatch for AcmeRetail) but that's risky. Better: force their DNS to prefer us-west VIP or adjust TGW/BGP local-pref so that the path to the us-west VIP wins.

sanjay-eng: I can put a temporary rollback in the routing plane: create a route override at the peering level to prefer us-west for their ASN/peer. Need approval from netops. maya-net can you advise exact CIDR they'd want pinned?

maya-net: Recommend pinning the customer's egress ASN prefixes to the us-west VIP 34.201.8.9/32 in the TGW RT for 24 hours while they validate. Also ask them to switch their resolver to 8.8.8.8 for a quick test to see if DNS fixes it.

dana-support: Customer asked for a repro they can show their infra team. Can we give them a short checklist with commands and the exact headers? I'll send it and escalate if they want a network call.

sanjay-eng: Checklist (short):
- curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -v (capture x-rr-region)
- dig +short api.redwood.example @<their-resolver>
- traceroute to the returned IP (paste last 4 hops)
- openssl s_client -servername api.redwood.example -connect <returned-ip>:443 | sed -n '1,10p' (check cert issuer)
- tcpdump on egress to confirm SNAT source IP

deploy-bot: deploy event: route-change-override request queued by sanjay-eng #deploy-req-445

dana-support: Thanks everyone — I'll send this to AcmeRetail and request the traceroute + dig output. If they confirm DNS -> eu, we'll schedule the TGW override and monitor for 24h. Escalating to Tier 2 netops now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

tom-cs: Please tag me on the support ticket when you have confirmation, I'll prep an interim billing credit request if their SLAs breached during the window.

sanjay-eng: Adding one last note — add a short-lived health-check route to their customer config so our health check targets prefer us-west during the test, that will help trigger our canary fallback if anything else breaks.

eli-onprem: Customer confirmed they swapped to 8.8.8.8 and calls now land in us-west. Will get their net team to open a TGW/BGP ticket to fix local-pref.

dana-support: Closing this thread for now, will reopen if routing override causes any regressions.
